checks.label: OverlayFS Active (adb remount)
checks.command:
M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no_mount_table"; else O=$(printf '%s
' "$M" | awk '$1=="overlay"{print ($2=="on")?$3:$2}' ); F=$(printf '%s
' "$O" | grep -xE '/|/system|/system_ext|/vendor|/product|/odm|/oem|/vendor_dlkm|/system_dlkm|/odm_dlkm' | tr '
' ' '); S=$(printf '%s
' "$M" | awk '{mp=($2=="on")?$3:$2; if(mp=="/mnt/scratch"||mp=="/cache/overlay") print mp}' | tr '
' ' '); N=$(printf '%s' "$F" | wc -w); T=$(printf '%s
' "$O" | grep -c .); echo "firmware_overlays=$N other_overlays=$((T-N)) firmware_paths=[$F] remount_scratch=[$S]"; fi
checks.description: OverlayFS mounted ON a firmware partition (/, /system, /system_ext, /vendor, /product, /odm, /oem, or a *_dlkm) means 'adb remount' or an equivalent overlay is active: read-only firmware becomes writable and dm-verity no longer covers what the running system reads. A /mnt/scratch or /cache/overlay mount is the persistent backing store adb remount creates and is reported alongside. Overlay mounts on any other path, notably container runtimes rooted under /data, are counted as other_overlays and do not affect firmware integrity.
checks.remediation: Only act when firmware_overlays is non-zero or remount_scratch is non-empty. Reboot to drop the overlay, then confirm every firmware partition mounts 'ro' again. If a scratch mount persists across reboot, run 'adb enable-verity' and reflash the affected partitions. A non-zero other_overlays with firmware_overlays=0 is normal on devices that run containers and needs no action.

checks.label: OverlayFS Mount Inventory
checks.command: M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no_mount_table"; else printf '%s\n' "$M" | awk '$1=="overlay"{print ($2=="on")?$3:$2}'  | head -20 | sed 's|^|overlay_at |'; echo "count=$(printf '%s\n' "$M" | awk '$1=="overlay"{c++}END{print c+0}')"; fi
checks.description: Every OverlayFS mount point on the device, so an analyst can see where each overlay actually sits instead of inferring intent from a bare count. Read this together with 'OverlayFS Active (adb remount)': that check decides severity, this one records the evidence behind it.
checks.remediation: Informational. Confirm each listed path is an expected container or runtime overlay. Any entry that is a firmware mount point is handled by the 'OverlayFS Active (adb remount)' check.

checks.label: Product Partition Writable
checks.command: mount 2>/dev/null | grep ' /product ' | grep -v 'ro,'
checks.description: /product partition is mounted read-write. Pre-installed product apps can be modified.
checks.remediation: Remount /product as read-only: 'mount -o remount,ro /product'. Reflash stock firmware to restore verity.

checks.label: ODM Partition Writable
checks.command: mount 2>/dev/null | grep ' /odm ' | grep -v 'ro,'
checks.description: /odm partition is mounted read-write. Device-manufacturer overlays can be tampered with.
checks.remediation: Remount /odm as read-only: 'mount -o remount,ro /odm'. Verify the build has dm-verity enabled for /odm.

checks.label: System_ext Partition Writable
checks.command: mount 2>/dev/null | grep ' /system_ext ' | grep -v 'ro,'
checks.description: /system_ext partition is mounted read-write. System extensions (carrier, OEM) can be modified.
checks.remediation: Remount /system_ext as read-only: 'mount -o remount,ro /system_ext'. Re-enable dm-verity.

checks.label: Persist Partition Writable
checks.command: mount 2>/dev/null | grep -E ' /persist | /mnt/vendor/persist ' | grep -v 'ro,'
checks.description: /persist holds calibration data, device IDs, and security tokens. Writable access allows tampering with hardware-bound credentials.
checks.remediation: Restrict write access to /persist to privileged system processes only. Remount read-only if not needed.

checks.label: Boot Partition Block Device
checks.command: P=$(ls -la /dev/block/by-name/boot /dev/block/bootdevice/by-name/boot 2>/dev/null | head -3); if [ -n "$P" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$P"; elif ls -d /dev/block/by-name/boot /dev/block/bootdevice/by-name/boot 2>&1 | grep -qi 'permission denied'; then echo UNMEASURED; else echo "ABSENT no boot by-name node"; fi
checks.description: Boot partition block device location and permissions
checks.remediation: Ensure boot partition block device is only accessible to root. Set permissions to 0600 or restrict via SELinux.

checks.label: Recovery Partition Block Permissions
checks.command: P=$(ls -la /dev/block/by-name/recovery /dev/block/bootdevice/by-name/recovery 2>/dev/null | head -3); if [ -n "$P" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$P"; elif ls -d /dev/block/by-name/recovery /dev/block/bootdevice/by-name/recovery 2>&1 | grep -qi 'permission denied'; then echo UNMEASURED; else echo "ABSENT no recovery partition (A/B device)"; fi
checks.description: Recovery partition should only be accessible to root (brw------- or 660 at most)
checks.remediation: Set block device permissions: 'chmod 600 /dev/block/by-name/recovery'. Enforce via udev/ueventd rules.

checks.label: Userdata Encryption Type
checks.command: getprop ro.crypto.type 2>/dev/null
checks.description: ro.crypto.type=file means File-Based Encryption (FBE) is active. 'block' means full-disk encryption (FDE, legacy). Missing means no encryption.
checks.remediation: Ensure the device uses FBE (ro.crypto.type=file). FDE is deprecated. Devices without encryption expose all user data.

checks.label: Userdata Encryption State
checks.command: getprop ro.crypto.state 2>/dev/null
checks.description: Userdata partition must be encrypted. 'unencrypted' means all app data is readable without authentication.
checks.remediation: Enable encryption via device policy (MDM) or reflash a firmware build with encryption enforced in fstab.

checks.label: dm-verity Devices Active
checks.command: V=$(ls /dev/block/mapper/ 2>/dev/null | grep -c -- '-verity'); if [ "$V" -gt 0 ]; then echo "count=$V"; ls /dev/block/mapper/ 2>/dev/null | grep -- '-verity' | sed 's/-verity$//' | sort; elif [ -d /dev/block/mapper ]; then echo 'count=0'; else echo 'UNMEASURED /dev/block/mapper not present'; fi
checks.description: Partitions actually protected by dm-verity, identified by their '<name>-verity' device-mapper node and listed by name. Counting /dev/block/dm-* instead is misleading: that includes APEX loop mappings and every dynamic partition, so it reports a large number on a device with no verity at all.
checks.remediation: Reflash stock vbmeta without --disable-verity to restore dm-verity device-mapper targets.

checks.label: dm-verity Disabled Flag in cmdline
checks.command: grep -c -E 'androidboot.veritymode=disabled|skip_initramfs|verity=0' /proc/cmdline
checks.description: Kernel cmdline disabling dm-verity allows unsigned modifications to system/vendor partitions.
checks.remediation: Remove disable-verity flags from BOARD_KERNEL_CMDLINE. Flash a signed vbmeta: 'fastboot flash vbmeta vbmeta.img'.

checks.label: noexec on /data Partition
checks.command: M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); D=$(printf '%s\n' "$M" | grep ' /data '); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no mount table readable"; elif [ -z "$D" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no /data entry in mount table"; else printf '%s\n' "$D" | grep -c 'noexec'; fi
checks.description: Android executes app code from /data (dalvik-cache, app native libraries), so /data cannot carry noexec on a stock build. Recorded for inventory only. The achievable /data mount controls are nosuid and nodev, checked separately.
checks.remediation: No action on stock Android: /data must permit execution. Confirm the nosuid and nodev checks for /data pass instead.

checks.label: nosuid on /data Partition
checks.command: M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); D=$(printf '%s\n' "$M" | grep ' /data '); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no mount table readable"; elif [ -z "$D" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no /data entry in mount table"; else printf '%s\n' "$D" | grep -c 'nosuid'; fi
checks.description: /data should be mounted nosuid to prevent setuid binaries placed by apps from gaining root. Missing nosuid is a privilege escalation vector.
checks.remediation: Add 'nosuid' to the fstab entry for /data and remount: 'mount -o remount,nosuid /data'.

checks.label: nodev on /data Partition
checks.command: M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); D=$(printf '%s\n' "$M" | grep ' /data '); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no mount table readable"; elif [ -z "$D" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no /data entry in mount table"; else printf '%s\n' "$D" | grep -c 'nodev'; fi
checks.description: /data should be mounted nodev to block device file creation (character/block devices) by unprivileged apps.
checks.remediation: Add 'nodev' to the fstab entry for /data and remount: 'mount -o remount,nodev /data'.

checks.label: A/B Active Slot
checks.command: getprop ro.boot.slot_suffix 2>/dev/null
checks.description: Active A/B slot suffix. A/B partitioning supports safe OTA rollback. Missing indicates non-A/B or single-slot device.
checks.remediation: Ensure the device is on the expected boot slot. If the wrong slot is active after an OTA, investigate for update failure.

checks.label: Inactive Slot Integrity
checks.command: getprop ro.boot.slot_suffix 2>/dev/null | grep -qE '^_[ab]$' && avbctl verify-partition --partition system 2>/dev/null || echo N/A
checks.description: Verify inactive slot partition integrity via avbctl (if available)
checks.remediation: If slot verification fails, re-flash the inactive slot from a known-good OTA package.

checks.label: Partition Table Type (GPT/MBR)
checks.command: cat /proc/partitions 2>/dev/null | head -20
checks.description: Partition table listing from kernel - review for unexpected entries
checks.remediation: Verify all listed partitions match the device's expected partition layout from the OEM.

checks.label: Userdata Filesystem Type
checks.command: mount 2>/dev/null | grep ' /data ' | awk '{print $5}' | head -1
checks.description: Userdata filesystem type (f2fs or ext4 expected). Other types may indicate tampering or unusual configurations.
checks.remediation: Reflash the userdata partition with the OEM-supplied format if the filesystem type is unexpected.

checks.label: Unexpected Loop Device Mounts
checks.command:
M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no_mount_table"; else L=$(printf '%s
' "$M" | awk '$1 ~ /^/dev/(block/)?loop/ {mp=($2=="on")?$3:$2; if (mp !~ /^/apex//) print mp}'); A=$(printf '%s
' "$M" | awk '$1 ~ /^/dev/(block/)?loop/ {mp=($2=="on")?$3:$2; if (mp ~ /^/apex//) c++} END{print c+0}'); N=$(printf '%s
' "$L" | grep -c .); echo "non_apex_loop=$N apex_loop=$A paths=[$(printf '%s' "$L" | tr '
' ' ')]"; fi
checks.description: A loop-mounted filesystem outside /apex/ can be a side-loaded image or a hidden filesystem. APEX Mainline modules are themselves loop mounts on Android 10+ and are excluded by mount point, not by count, so a normal device reports non_apex_loop=0 with a non-zero apex_loop.
checks.remediation: Identify each path in paths=[] and the image behind it (losetup -a, or readlink the backing file). Unmount and remove any image that is not part of the shipping build. A non-zero apex_loop on its own is normal.

checks.label: APEX Partitions Mounted
checks.command: mount 2>/dev/null | grep -c '/apex/'
checks.description: APEX partitions should be present on Android 10+ for Mainline modules
checks.remediation: If APEX partitions are missing on Android 10+, verify the APEX service is running and the build supports Mainline.

checks.label: Block Devices World-Readable
checks.command: find /dev/block -maxdepth 3 -type b -perm -o+r | wc -l
checks.description: Block-device NODES readable by all users allow unprivileged processes to read raw partition data including encryption keys and user data. Restricted with -type b so it counts actual block special files only - the previous command counted the o+r symlinks and directories under /dev/block (by-name, mapper, param, persistent ...), which are harmless and produced a large false count.
checks.remediation: Remove world-read from block devices: 'chmod o-r /dev/block/<device>'. Enforce via ueventd.rc rules.

checks.label: Userdata Partition Used Space
checks.command: df /data 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==2{print $5}'
checks.description: Userdata partition usage - extremely high usage (>95%) can cause system instability and logging failures
checks.remediation: Free space on /data by clearing app caches, removing unused apps, or factory resetting as last resort.

checks.label: fstab Encryption Required
checks.command: P="/vendor/etc/fstab.* /odm/etc/fstab.* /system/etc/fstab.* /etc/fstab* /first_stage_ramdisk/fstab.*"; D=$(cat $P 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#' | grep -E '[[:space:]]/data[[:space:]]'); G=$(cat /proc/device-tree/firmware/android/fstab/userdata/fsmgr_flags 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\000'); S=$(grep -lE '[[:space:]]/data[[:space:]]' $P 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' '); [ -n "$G" ] && S="$S device-tree"; A="$D $G"; if [ -z "$D$G" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no_readable_data_fstab_entry"; else case "$A" in *fileencryption=*) E=fbe ;; *forceencrypt*|*forcefdeorfbe*) E=fde ;; *encryptable=*) E=encryptable_only ;; *) E=none ;; esac; case "$A" in *metadata_encryption=*) M=yes ;; *) M=no ;; esac; echo "data_encryption=$E metadata=$M src=[$S]"; fi
checks.description: The /data entry in the fstab must request encryption. fileencryption= is FBE (Android 10+), forceencrypt/forcefdeorfbe is legacy FDE, and encryptable= alone only permits encryption without requiring it. Searched in /vendor/etc, /odm/etc, /system/etc, /etc and the first-stage ramdisk, plus the device-tree fstab node that many SoCs use instead of a file. When no /data entry is readable the check reports UNMEASURED rather than asserting encryption is missing: on that device the runtime answer comes from 'Userdata Encryption State' (ro.crypto.state) and 'Userdata Encryption Type' (ro.crypto.type), which measure effect rather than policy.
checks.remediation: On data_encryption=none or encryptable_only, add 'fileencryption=aes-256-xts:aes-256-cts' (and 'metadata_encryption=aes-256-xts' for metadata encryption) to the /data entry and rebuild the vendor image. On UNMEASURED, read the fstab from the boot or vendor_boot ramdisk offline, and confirm ro.crypto.state is 'encrypted' on the running device.

checks.label: Cache Partition Present
checks.command: mount 2>/dev/null | grep ' /cache ' | head -1
checks.description: Cache partition used for OTA staging. Present on legacy A-only devices; absent on A/B devices is normal.
checks.remediation: On A-only devices, ensure /cache is mounted and accessible for OTA updates. On A/B devices, absence is expected.

checks.label: Unlocked Critical Partitions
checks.command: V=$(grep -hoE 'androidboot\.verifiedbootstate=[a-z]+|androidboot\.verifiedbootstate = "[a-z]+' /proc/cmdline /proc/bootconfig 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[a-z]+$' | head -1); [ -z "$V" ] && V=$(getprop ro.boot.verifiedbootstate 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$V" ]; then echo "androidboot.verifiedbootstate=$V"; fi
checks.description: verifiedbootstate: green=fully verified, yellow=self-signed (custom root of trust), orange=unlocked, red=failed. Non-green allows partition tampering. Reads /proc/cmdline, /proc/bootconfig (Android 12+ may export androidboot.* via bootconfig) and falls back to getprop ro.boot.verifiedbootstate.
checks.remediation: Lock the bootloader and flash OEM-signed partitions to achieve verifiedbootstate=green.

checks.label: Metadata Partition Accessible
checks.command: if ls /dev/block/by-name/metadata >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo present; elif ! ls /dev/block/by-name >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "UNMEASURED /dev/block/by-name not listable"; else echo absent; fi
checks.description: Metadata partition stores FBE/FDE keys and state. Required for encrypted userdata on Android 9+.
checks.remediation: Ensure the metadata partition exists in the partition table. Absence on Android 9+ means encryption keys may not persist.

checks.label: Sideloading Partition (ota_package)
checks.command: find /data/ota_package -type f | head -5; ls /cache/*.zip /tmp/*.zip 2>/dev/null | head -5
checks.description: Staged OTA or sideload packages left on disk. The /data/ota_package directory itself is standard on Android and is not reported; only files staged inside it or .zip packages in /cache or /tmp are.
checks.remediation: Remove unknown update packages: 'rm /data/ota_package/*'. Only stage OTA packages from trusted update servers.

checks.label: noexec on /storage/emulated User Storage
checks.command: M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no mount table readable"; else out=$(printf '%s\n' "$M" | grep ' /storage/emulated '); if [ -n "$out" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'noexec' && echo OK || echo MISSING; else echo NA; fi; fi
checks.description: User-facing storage (the modern /sdcard at /storage/emulated) should be mounted noexec. Apps and attackers commonly drop binaries here; without noexec they can be executed directly. NA means the path is not mounted on this device.
checks.remediation: Add 'noexec' to the fstab entry for /storage/emulated and remount: 'mount -o remount,noexec /storage/emulated'.

checks.label: nosuid on /storage/emulated User Storage
checks.command: M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no mount table readable"; else out=$(printf '%s\n' "$M" | grep ' /storage/emulated '); if [ -n "$out" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'nosuid' && echo OK || echo MISSING; else echo NA; fi; fi
checks.description: User storage must be nosuid. A missing nosuid flag lets a planted setuid root binary keep its privileges when executed from user storage, a direct privilege-escalation path. NA means the path is not mounted on this device.
checks.remediation: Add 'nosuid' to the fstab entry for /storage/emulated and remount: 'mount -o remount,nosuid /storage/emulated'.

checks.label: noexec on /mnt/media_rw (USB OTG)
checks.command: M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no mount table readable"; else out=$(printf '%s\n' "$M" | grep ' /mnt/media_rw '); if [ -n "$out" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'noexec' && echo OK || echo MISSING; else echo NA; fi; fi
checks.description: USB OTG storage mounted under /mnt/media_rw must be noexec to stop malware on inserted drives from executing. NA means no USB storage is currently attached.
checks.remediation: Add 'noexec' to the fstab entry for /mnt/media_rw and remount: 'mount -o remount,noexec /mnt/media_rw'.

checks.label: nosuid on /mnt/media_rw (USB OTG)
checks.command: M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no mount table readable"; else out=$(printf '%s\n' "$M" | grep ' /mnt/media_rw '); if [ -n "$out" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'nosuid' && echo OK || echo MISSING; else echo NA; fi; fi
checks.description: USB storage must be nosuid; a setuid binary on a USB drive must not retain root when executed. NA means no USB storage is currently attached.
checks.remediation: Add 'nosuid' to the fstab entry for /mnt/media_rw and remount: 'mount -o remount,nosuid /mnt/media_rw'.

checks.label: noexec on /cache
checks.command: M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no mount table readable"; else out=$(printf '%s\n' "$M" | grep ' /cache '); if [ -n "$out" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'noexec' && echo OK || echo MISSING; else echo NA; fi; fi
checks.description: /cache is writable scratch space. Without noexec, dropped binaries can be executed. NA means /cache is not a separate partition on this device (common on A/B devices that have removed /cache).
checks.remediation: Add 'noexec' to the fstab entry for /cache and remount: 'mount -o remount,noexec /cache'.

checks.label: nosuid on /cache
checks.command: M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no mount table readable"; else out=$(printf '%s\n' "$M" | grep ' /cache '); if [ -n "$out" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'nosuid' && echo OK || echo MISSING; else echo NA; fi; fi
checks.description: /cache must be nosuid to prevent setuid escalation from this writable region. NA means /cache is not a separate partition on this device.
checks.remediation: Add 'nosuid' to the fstab entry for /cache and remount: 'mount -o remount,nosuid /cache'.

checks.label: noexec on /metadata
checks.command:
M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); out=$(printf '%s
' "$M" | grep ' /metadata '); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no mount table readable"; elif [ -z "$out" ]; then echo NA; elif printf '%s
' "$out" | grep -q 'noexec'; then echo OK; else echo "MISSING"; printf '%s
' "$out"; fi
checks.description: /metadata stores file-based encryption metadata and should never need to execute binaries. NA means the device has no metadata partition (older A-only devices).
checks.remediation: Add 'noexec' to the fstab entry for /metadata and remount: 'mount -o remount,noexec /metadata'.

checks.label: nosuid on /metadata
checks.command:
M=$(cat /proc/mounts 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$M" ] || M=$(mount 2>/dev/null); out=$(printf '%s
' "$M" | grep ' /metadata '); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "UNMEASURED no mount table readable"; elif [ -z "$out" ]; then echo NA; elif printf '%s
' "$out" | grep -q 'nosuid'; then echo OK; else echo "MISSING"; printf '%s
' "$out"; fi
checks.description: /metadata must be nosuid; it is writable and a setuid binary placed there must not gain privilege. NA means the device has no metadata partition.
checks.remediation: Add 'nosuid' to the fstab entry for /metadata and remount: 'mount -o remount,nosuid /metadata'.

checks.label: APEX Active Versions and Rollback State
checks.command: A=$(cmd -w apexservice getActivePackages 2>/dev/null | head -12); case "$A" in ""|*"Can't find service"*|*"Failure calling service"*|*"Failed transaction"*|*"Found 0 services"*) A="";; esac; [ -z "$A" ] && A=$(ls -d /apex/*/ 2>/dev/null | sed 's#/apex/##;s#/##' | grep -v '@' | head -12 | tr '\n' ' '); S=$(ls -d /apex/*@* 2>/dev/null | wc -l); [ -z "$A" ] && echo "UNMEASURED apexservice silent and /apex not listable" || echo "apex=$A staged=$S"
checks.description: Lists the active APEX modules and how many versioned mount points are present. APEX delivers updatable system components (ART, conscrypt, media, DNS resolver, tethering) outside the full OTA, each signed independently and verified at activation. The security question is which version is actually active: a module rolled back or pinned to an older build reintroduces whatever it had been patched for, and a versioned mount left behind indicates a staged or reverted activation. The existing APEX checks cover signing and mount state; none covered the active version set.
checks.remediation: Compare the active module versions against the expected set for this build and security patch level. Investigate any module pinned below the platform version, since APEX modules carry their own security fixes independent of the OTA.

checks.label: Filesystem Repair Tool Permissions
checks.command: T=''; for b in /system/bin/e2fsck /system/bin/fsck.f2fs /system/bin/fsck_msdos /system/bin/tune2fs /system/bin/make_f2fs /system/bin/mke2fs; do [ -e "$b" ] && T="$T $(ls -l $b 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1" "$NF}')"; done; W=$(find /system/bin -maxdepth 1 \( -name 'fsck*' -o -name '*e2fs*' -o -name '*f2fs*' \) -perm -o+w 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' '); [ -n "$W" ] && echo "FSCK_TOOL_WORLD_WRITABLE $W" || { [ -z "$T" ] && echo NO_FSCK_TOOLS || echo "FSCK_TOOLS_PRESENT$T"; }
checks.description: Reports the filesystem repair and formatting tools present on the system partition and whether any is world-writable. These binaries run early in boot with high privilege and parse attacker-influenceable on-disk structures, so a malformed superblock on removable media or on a partition an attacker can reach becomes a parsing bug in a privileged context. A world-writable repair tool is a direct code-replacement path into early boot.
checks.remediation: Remove write permission from any tool listed and confirm the system partition is mounted read-only. Remove formatting tools such as mke2fs and make_f2fs from production images that never reformat.
checks.why: Repair tools parse untrusted on-disk structures with high privilege during early boot.
checks.risk_if_fail: A writable repair binary is executed with privilege during boot, giving code execution before Android starts.

checks.label: Dynamic (Logical) Partition Inventory
checks.command:
M=$(ls /dev/block/mapper/ 2>/dev/null | grep -vE -- '-verity|by-uuid|^com\.android\.' | sort); D=$(getprop ro.boot.dynamic_partitions 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$M" ]; then echo "dynamic=${D:-unset} logical=none"; else echo "dynamic=${D:-unset} count=$(printf '%s
' "$M" | grep -c .)"; printf '%s
' "$M" | tr '
' ' '; echo; fi
checks.description: Logical partitions carved out of the super partition on devices using dynamic partitioning. Lists them by name, including both A/B copies where present. An unexpected logical partition is a repartitioning indicator that a check reading only /proc/partitions cannot see, because logical partitions appear as device-mapper nodes rather than as physical partitions.
checks.remediation: Compare the logical partition set against the expected set for this build. Investigate any name that is not a standard Android partition or its _a/_b pair.
checks.why: Dynamic partitions are invisible to a physical partition table listing.
checks.risk_if_fail: A partition added or resized inside super goes unreported.
